title: Finding your doppelganger
titleChinese: 寻找长相酷似你的那个人
paragraphs: What is the likelihood of you having someone who looks just like you? Would it be a good thing? And if you did have one, would you want to meet them?

Consider how often your facial features are used to identify you. Your passport, ID card and driving licence all bare your face. To enter your workplace, you likely need to be recognisable. You may need your face to unlock your smartphone and possibly even need it to exclude you from being present at a crime scene.

The word ‘doppelganger’ refers to a person who looks the same as you, essentially sharing your features; those that you thought were unique to you and your identity. Not an identical twin, as a doppelganger has no relation to you. The idea originated in German folklore. A doppelganger was said to be a spirit-double that replicated every human and beast on earth.

So, let’s get real. What are the chances of you having one in the first place? There’s said to be a one in 135 chance of an absolute dead ringer for you existing anywhere in the world, so the chances are pretty low, despite folk wisdom promising you otherwise. And the chances of meeting? The mathematical certainty of finding this particular person is supposedly less than one in a trillion!

That said, these statistics may be a good thing. Historically, having a double hasn’t always been a positive. Back in 1999, an innocent American man, indistinguishable from the real criminal, was sent to prison for robbery, where he stayed for 19 years. In the end, it turned out to be a case of mistaken identity. In a different case, a woman in New York was accused of trying to poison her doppelganger with deadly cheesecake so that she could steal her identity!

And, why are people interested in finding their possible doppelganger anyway? It may be helpful to look to the past when facial resemblance indicated kinship. Maybe one day you’ll meet your lookalike, but we understand that, after this, you possibly don’t want to!

vocabulary.entry: likelihood /ˈlaɪklihʊd/ n. 可能性；可能发生的事
vocabulary.example: There is a high likelihood of rain later today.
vocabulary.translation: 今天晚些时候下雨的可能性很大。

vocabulary.entry: facial features /ˈfeɪʃl ˈfiːtʃəz/ n. 面部特征；五官
vocabulary.example: Her facial features are very similar to her mother's.
vocabulary.translation: 她的五官和她母亲的十分相似。

vocabulary.entry: exclude /ɪkˈskluːd/ v. 把……排除在外；不包括；免除
vocabulary.example: This evidence cannot be excluded from the investigation.
vocabulary.translation: 这项证据不能被排除在调查之外。

vocabulary.entry: crime scene /ˈkraɪm siːn/ n. 犯罪现场
vocabulary.example: Police officers arrived quickly to secure the crime scene.
vocabulary.translation: 警察迅速赶到并封锁了犯罪现场。

vocabulary.entry: doppelganger /ˈdɒpəlɡæŋə(r)/ n. 面貌酷似的人；分身（词源为德语）
vocabulary.example: She met her doppelganger on a trip to Paris and was shocked by the resemblance.
vocabulary.translation: 她在巴黎旅行时遇到了和自己长得一模一样的人，被那相似度惊呆了。

vocabulary.entry: essentially /ɪˈsenʃəli/ adv. 本质上；根本上；基本上
vocabulary.example: The two ideas are essentially the same, just expressed differently.
vocabulary.translation: 这两个想法本质上是一样的，只是表达形式不同。

vocabulary.entry: unique /juːˈniːk/ adj. 独有的；唯一的；独一无二的
vocabulary.example: Each person's fingerprint is unique to themselves.
vocabulary.translation: 每个人的指纹都是独一无二的。

vocabulary.entry: identical twin /aɪˈdentɪkl twɪn/ n. 同卵双胞胎；单卵双胞胎
vocabulary.example: Identical twins develop from a single fertilized egg and share the same genes.
vocabulary.translation: 同卵双胞胎由同一个受精卵发育而成，拥有相同的基因。

vocabulary.entry: originate /əˈrɪdʒɪneɪt/ v. 起源于；发源于；首创
vocabulary.example: This custom is believed to have originated in ancient China.
vocabulary.translation: 这个习俗被认为起源于中国古代。

vocabulary.entry: German folklore /ˈdʒɜːmən ˈfəʊklɔː(r)/ n. 德国民间传说
vocabulary.example: Many magical creatures appear in German folklore.
vocabulary.translation: 德国民间传说中出现了许多神奇的生物。

vocabulary.entry: spirit-double /ˈspɪrɪt dʌbl/ n. 灵体分身；灵魂复制品
vocabulary.example: The story tells of a knight who encounters his own spirit-double in a dark forest.
vocabulary.translation: 这个故事讲述了一位骑士在黑暗的森林中遇到了自己的灵体分身。

vocabulary.entry: replicate /ˈreplɪkeɪt/ v. 复制；复刻；精确再现
vocabulary.example: The artist tried to replicate the famous painting as accurately as possible.
vocabulary.translation: 这位艺术家试图尽可能精确地复刻这幅名画。

vocabulary.entry: get real /ɡet riːəl/ 认清现实；面对现实（口语）
vocabulary.example: You need to get real and stop dreaming about becoming a star overnight.
vocabulary.translation: 你得认清现实，别再做一夜成名的梦了。

vocabulary.entry: dead ringer /ˈded rɪŋə(r)/ n. 面貌酷似的人；一模一样的人（口语）
vocabulary.example: He's a dead ringer for the famous actor—people often stop him for photos.
vocabulary.translation: 他和那位著名演员长得一模一样，人们经常拦住他拍照。

vocabulary.entry: folk wisdom /ˈfəʊk ˈwɪzdəm/ n. 民间智慧；民间常识
vocabulary.example: Folk wisdom says that an apple a day keeps the doctor away.
vocabulary.translation: 民间常言道，一天一苹果，医生远离我。

vocabulary.entry: mathematical certainty /ˌmæθəˈmætɪkl ˈsɜːtnti/ n. 数学上的必然性；绝对的数学概率
vocabulary.example: There is no mathematical certainty that the plan will succeed.
vocabulary.translation: 这个计划能否成功在数学上没有绝对的必然性。

vocabulary.entry: supposedly /səˈpəʊzɪdli/ adv. 据说；据称；被认为
vocabulary.example: The treasure is supposedly hidden in a cave in the mountains.
vocabulary.translation: 据说宝藏藏在山里的一个洞穴里。

vocabulary.entry: trillion /ˈtrɪljən/ num. 万亿；兆（英式为10¹⁸，美式为10¹²）
vocabulary.example: The country's national debt is now over one trillion dollars.
vocabulary.translation: 这个国家的国债现在已超过一万亿美元。

vocabulary.entry: statistics /stəˈtɪstɪks/ n. 统计数据；统计学
vocabulary.example: The statistics show a sharp rise in unemployment over the past year.
vocabulary.translation: 统计数据显示，过去一年的失业率大幅上升。

vocabulary.entry: historically /hɪˈstɒrɪkli/ adv. 从历史角度看；历来；在历史上
vocabulary.example: This region has historically been a center of trade and culture.
vocabulary.translation: 这个地区历来是贸易和文化中心。

vocabulary.entry: indistinguishable /ˌɪndɪˈstɪŋɡwɪʃəbl/ adj. 难以区分的；无法分辨的；一模一样的
vocabulary.example: The two paintings are so similar that they are almost indistinguishable.
vocabulary.translation: 这两幅画如此相似，几乎难以分辨。

vocabulary.entry: mistaken identity /mɪˈsteɪkən aɪˈdentəti/ n. 认错人；身份误认
vocabulary.example: He was arrested by mistake due to a case of mistaken identity.
vocabulary.translation: 由于被认错人，他无辜被捕了。

vocabulary.entry: accuse /əˈkjuːz/ v. 控告；指控；指责
vocabulary.example: She was accused of stealing money from the company.
vocabulary.translation: 她被指控从公司偷钱。

vocabulary.entry: poison /ˈpɔɪzn/ v. 毒害；下毒；使中毒 n. 毒药；毒物
vocabulary.example: Someone tried to poison the king's food with a deadly chemical.
vocabulary.translation: 有人试图用一种致命的化学物质在国王的食物里下毒。

vocabulary.entry: facial resemblance /ˈfeɪʃl rɪˈzembləns/ n. 面部相似；长相相像
vocabulary.example: The facial resemblance between the father and son is striking.
vocabulary.translation: 这对父子的长相相似度惊人。

vocabulary.entry: kinship /ˈkɪnʃɪp/ n. 亲属关系；血缘关系；亲密关系
vocabulary.example: They felt a strong sense of kinship even though they were not related by blood.
vocabulary.translation: 尽管没有血缘关系，他们却感到一种强烈的亲密感。

vocabulary.entry: lookalike /ˈlʊkəlaɪk/ n. 面貌酷似的人（口语）
vocabulary.example: He works as a celebrity lookalike at parties and events.
vocabulary.translation: 他在派对和活动上做名人模仿秀，扮演和名人长得一模一样的人。

sentences.english: What is the likelihood of you having someone who looks just like you?
sentences.chinese: 世间有和你长得一模一样的人的可能性有多大？

sentences.english: Would it be a good thing?
sentences.chinese: 这会是好事吗？

sentences.english: And if you did have one, would you want to meet them?
sentences.chinese: 如果真有这样的一个人，你会想要和他见面吗？

sentences.english: Consider how often your facial features are used to identify you.
sentences.chinese: 不妨想想，你的面部特征有多么频繁地被用来识别你的身份。

sentences.english: Your passport, ID card and driving licence all bare your face.
sentences.chinese: 护照、身份证和驾照上，都印有你的面部照片。

sentences.english: To enter your workplace, you likely need to be recognisable. You may need your face to unlock your smartphone and possibly even need it to exclude you from being present at a crime scene.
sentences.chinese: 进入工作场所时，你需要被认出身份才能通行；解锁智能手机时，可能需要用到面部识别；甚至在排查犯罪现场嫌疑人时，你的面部特征也能帮你洗清嫌疑。

sentences.english: The word ‘doppelganger’ refers to a person who looks the same as you, essentially sharing your features; those that you thought were unique to you and your identity.
sentences.chinese: “分身（doppelganger）”这个词，指的是和你长得一模一样的人——你们有着几乎完全相同的面部特征，而这些特征你曾以为是独属于你、标识自身身份的东西。

sentences.english: Not an identical twin, as a doppelganger has no relation to you.
sentences.chinese: 但分身和同卵双胞胎不同，他们和你没有任何血缘关系。

sentences.english: The idea originated in German folklore. A doppelganger was said to be a spirit-double that replicated every human and beast on earth.
sentences.chinese: 这个概念起源于德国民间传说，传说中，分身是一种灵体复制品，世界上的每个人和每一种动物，都有一个对应的分身。

sentences.english: So, let’s get real.
sentences.chinese: 那么，让我们看看现实情况。

sentences.english: What are the chances of you having one in the first place?
sentences.chinese: 首先，你拥有一个分身的概率到底有多少？

sentences.english: There’s said to be a one in 135 chance of an absolute dead ringer for you existing anywhere in the world, so the chances are pretty low, despite folk wisdom promising you otherwise.
sentences.chinese: 据说，在全世界范围内存在一个和你长得一模一样的人的概率，仅为1/135，这个几率相当低，尽管民间说法说的可不是这么回事。

sentences.english: And the chances of meeting?
sentences.chinese: 而相遇的概率呢？

sentences.english: The mathematical certainty of finding this particular person is supposedly less than one in a trillion!
sentences.chinese: 从数学角度计算，找到这个特定之人的概率，据说还不到万亿分之一！

sentences.english: That said, these statistics may be a good thing.
sentences.chinese: 尽管如此，这样的概率或许反而是件好事。

sentences.english: Historically, having a double hasn’t always been a positive.
sentences.chinese: 从历史来看，拥有一个和自己长相一样的人，并非总是好事。

sentences.english: Back in 1999, an innocent American man, indistinguishable from the real criminal, was sent to prison for robbery, where he stayed for 19 years. In the end, it turned out to be a case of mistaken identity.
sentences.chinese: 早在1999年，一名无辜的美国男子因和真正的劫匪长得毫无差别，被误判抢劫罪入狱，刑期长达19年，最终证实这是一桩身份误认案件。

sentences.english: In a different case, a woman in New York was accused of trying to poison her doppelganger with deadly cheesecake so that she could steal her identity!
sentences.chinese: 还有另一个案例，纽约一名女子被指控试图用有毒的芝士蛋糕毒害自己的分身，目的竟是为了窃取对方的身份！

sentences.english: And, why are people interested in finding their possible doppelganger anyway?
sentences.chinese: 那么，人们为什么会对寻找自己可能存在的分身感兴趣呢？

sentences.english: It may be helpful to look to the past when facial resemblance indicated kinship.
sentences.chinese: 或许我们可以回溯到过去——在那个年代，面容相似往往意味着血缘关系。

sentences.english: Maybe one day you’ll meet your lookalike, but we understand that, after this, you possibly don’t want to!
sentences.chinese: 也许有一天，你真的会遇到和自己长得一模一样的人，但看完这些案例后，你可能就不会再期待这件事了！
